questions.stem: Concerning the gonadal activity of both sexes, which statement(s) is (are) correct?
options: In women this activity is cyclic, whereas in men it is discontinuous
The male gonadal sex needs the hormone AMH for its differentiation
Oogonia are observed in the cortical zone of the embryonic ovary
questions.explanation: No official answer key for this exam — answers worked out from the course.

questions.stem: Among the following statements about germ cells, which is (are) correct?
options: Spermatogonia are active from puberty onward
Primary oocytes appear during intrauterine life
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: The antral (cavitary) follicle is characterized by:
options: Progressive enlargement of the follicular cavity
questions.explanation: No official key — the mature pre-ovulatory follicle is the Graafian follicle.

questions.stem: Concerning oogenesis, the differentiation phase:
options: Designates the transformation of primary oocytes into secondary oocytes
Results in a stock of 300 million primary oocytes
questions.explanation: No official key — differentiation (oogonia → primary oocytes) occurs in fetal life; the peak stock is about 7 million.

questions.stem:
The uterine cycle is characterized by cyclic changes of the uterine mucosa over an average of 28 days, alternating destruction and reconstruction. Order these events chronologically:
A – formation of the "uterine lace": arteries become spiral and glands long and tortuous
B – menstrual period: endometrium very thin due to its destruction
C – secretory phase = glycogen production to nourish the embryo; the endometrium reaches its maximal thickness and prepares to receive the embryo
D – the endometrium regenerates and proliferates, with tubular gland elongation and blood vessel development
questions.explanation: No official key — proliferative phase, secretory phase, uterine lace (premenstrual), then menstruation.

questions.stem: Which hormonal event triggers ovulation?
options: The concomitant rise of estrogens and progesterone
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: The menstrual cycle is defined by the succession:
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: During ovulation:
options: The primary oocyte becomes a secondary oocyte with emission of the 1st polar body
The primary oocyte divides into two identical cells
The secondary oocyte is released from the ovary to be picked up by the uterine tube
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: The corpus luteum:
options: Receives a hormonal signal to persist in case of fertilization
questions.explanation: No official key — hCG maintains it.

questions.stem: The enzymatic equipment of the acrosome:
options: Is at the origin of the "cortical reaction"
Allows dissolution of the envelope of the secondary oocyte, i.e. the Slavjanski membrane
Is at the origin of the acrosome reaction
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Amphimixis (karyogamy):
options: Designates the fusion of the male and female pronuclei into a single nucleus
Is defined as the two-blastomere stage of the egg
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Fertilization has the following consequence(s):
options: The 2nd physiological awakening of the egg
Determination of the genetic sex of the egg, which depends on the sex chromosome carried by the oocyte
questions.explanation: No official key — genetic sex depends on the spermatozoon; fertilization restores diploidy.

questions.stem: Among the anterior pituitary hormones listed below, which is (are) active on ovarian function?
questions.explanation: No official key — hCG is placental, not pituitary.

questions.stem: About the reaction of the endometrium to implantation:
options: It occurs on day 7 and starts at the implantation zone in contact with the syncytiotrophoblast
It is an immunological reaction: invasion by lymphocytes with increased vascularization
It is also called the acrosomal reaction
Stromal cells become larger, fill with glycogen and lipids and form decidual cells
questions.explanation: No official key — this is the decidual reaction.

questions.stem: For implantation to succeed, which condition(s) must be met?
options: The endometrium must be ready to be colonized by the embryonic trophoblast
It is a true graft that can only succeed thanks to the "anti-rejection" action of the trophoblast, which tends to "mask" embryonic antigens
Implantation can only occur during a normal cycle around day 15
When the mucosa has received ideal hormonal stimulation, essentially FSH and LH
questions.explanation: No official key — the implantation window is around day 20–21, under estrogen and progesterone.

questions.stem: About the primitive streak, which assertion(s) is (are) correct? It:
options: Is set up at the beginning of the 3rd week of development
Forms a cellular groove along the cephalo-caudal axis of the embryo
Is bounded posteriorly by Hensen's node
Is followed by the appearance of the mesoblast
questions.explanation: No official key — Hensen's node is at its cranial end.

questions.stem:
Put in exact chronological order the events of the 3rd week of embryonic development:
A – appearance of a depression marking a primitive streak
B – formation of a dorsal notochord
C – ectoblast cells with mesoblastic potential are formed
D – a median thickening of the ectoblast marks the start of neurulation
Choose the right combination:
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Among these hormones, which is (are) NOT secreted by the placenta during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: At which developmental period does the amniotic cavity form?
options: At the beginning of the 2nd week of development
When the third germ layer forms
questions.explanation: No official key — around day 8.

questions.stem: Which statement(s) about the diagram (figure) is (are) correct?
options: It is an embryo at the trabecular (lacunar) stage
Arrow 2 points to the uterine cavity
Arrow 3 points to the follicular cavity
The didermic disc lies between two cavities
questions.explanation: No official key — the didermic disc lies between the amniotic cavity and the primary yolk sac.

questions.stem: About the second week of embryonic development, it:
options: Leads to the formation of a didermic embryo
Marks the establishment of blood exchanges between the mother and the embryo
At its end, is characterized by a pre-gastrulation phenomenon
questions.explanation: No official key — blastulation is week 1; the prechordal plate appears at the end of week 2.

questions.stem: Among the following statements about somites, which is (are) correct?
options: They originate from the intermediate mesoblast
They start to appear in the posterior dorsal region of the embryo
The first pairs appear on day 21
questions.explanation: No official key — somites come from paraxial mesoderm, appear in the occipital region from about day 20.

questions.stem: Concerning the allantois:
options: It is a diverticulum formed by invagination of the endoderm
The allantoic epithelium is lined by extra-embryonic mesenchyme forming the splanchnopleure
The intra-embryonic (proximal) part regresses rapidly before the end of the 3rd week
The extra-embryonic (distal) part is a constituent of the umbilical cord
questions.explanation: No official key — the proximal part persists as the urachus.

questions.stem: Among the embryological elements below, which undergo an inductive effect from other embryological structures?
questions.explanation: No official key — the neural tube is induced by the notochord.

questions.stem: At which developmental stages can monozygotic twins form?
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: What is the approximate age of an embryo with 12 pairs of somites?
questions.explanation: No official key — the closest option.

questions.stem: Which statement(s) about the diagram (figure) is (are) correct?
options: It shows the process of spermatogenesis
It shows the division of a spermatid into a spermatozoon
The enzymatic capital is contained in the acrosome
The energy capital is contained in the end piece of the flagellum
questions.explanation: No official key — the figure shows spermiogenesis (part of spermatogenesis), a transformation, not a division; mitochondria are in the middle piece.

questions.stem: Among the following elements, which enter into the constitution of the placenta?
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: Among the characteristics of the embryonic annexes, which is (are) correct? They:
options: Form independently of the fertilized oocyte
Have the same karyotype and genotype as the embryo/fetus
Appear late because the human egg is alecithal
questions.explanation: No official key.

questions.stem: The "most identical" identical twins have the following characteristic(s):
questions.explanation: No official key.
